speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please tell me, which specific antibiotic were you prescribed and taking before these symptoms of fever, itching, and joint pain began?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Amoxicillin-induced morbilliform drug eruption with arthralgia. The clinical presentation of a pruritic rash appearing on the trunk and extremities following antibiotic therapy for sinusitis, accompanied by low-grade fever and joint pain, is highly suggestive of a hypersensitivity reaction. No further tests are required at this time.
